system.name: DUB (Discrete Unit Back-translation)
system.one_liner: Back-translation for direct speech translation: speech becomes discrete units so a text-to-unit model can synthesise extra training pairs for the unit-to-text model.

content.variant_note: panel (b) puts four circled steps in the quadrants of a cross-ruled box, linked by block and curved arrows; panel (a) is a bottom-up model sketch
content.argues: Representing speech as discrete units lets back-translation, a text-side technique, work for direct speech translation: a text-to-unit model turns extra target text into synthetic units that train the unit-to-text model.
content.subject: A speech-to-units-to-text model structure, and the four steps of discrete unit back-translation with stacked data cards.

summary: DUB applies back-translation to direct speech translation by first turning speech into discrete units. Figure 1 has two panels. In (a), speech passes an offline extractor (HuBERT, K-means, then a Deduplicate step) to give a unit sequence u, which a unit-to-text model turns into the German translation y and a text-to-unit model turns back. In (b), four circled steps sit in the quadrants of a cross-ruled box: prepare the unit-translation pairs, train the text-to-unit model, generate pseudo pairs tagged <BT> from extra target text, and train the unit-to-text model on real and pseudo pairs. Data sets are offset stacks of coloured cards, with red dashes around the pseudo data.
summary_zh: DUB 先把语音转成离散单元再做回译。图 1 左为模型结构：离线抽取器（HuBERT、K-means、去重）得到单元序列，连接 U2T 与 T2U；右为四步训练流程，按象限排布，用彩色卡片堆表示真实与伪数据，红虚线框标出伪数据。
notes: Prior labels kept (stage-pipeline, model-anatomy). Example values (unit IDs, short words) are illustrative; the cards in (b) carry the same pink unit and lilac text cards as the real pair. The dashed outlines are filled dash paths in the SVG, not stroke-dasharray, which is why the digest counts no dashed shapes. The gradient fills of the model boxes are not in the histogram, so their hex values are read off the picture (approx).
